summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, atrial fibrillation, esophageal stricture, and alcohol abuse was admitted after a fall at home associated with vomiting, tachycardia, and hypoxia. He was found to have aspiration pneumonia, likely due to his known swallowing dysfunction and esophageal abnormalities. Atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response resolved spontaneously but required rate control with increased diltiazem. He underwent esophageal dilation for a symptomatic stricture and was transitioned from IV to oral antibiotics. His hypothyroidism was addressed with an increased levothyroxine dose, and iron supplementation was started for anemia. He improved clinically, was weaned off oxygen, and tolerated a regular diet. He was discharged home with services on a full course of antibiotics, adjusted medications, and follow-up plans for thyroid testing and colonoscopy.
problems: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food or vomitus
Fall from other slipping, tripping, or stumbling
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Diaphragmatic hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
